title_as_printed: Experimental Results of Boiling Point Elevation of Simulated Sea Water (SSW)
pressure_note: Boiling point elevation at the vapor pressure of the solution (equal to vapor pressure of pure water at 'Boiling Temperature for Pure Water'); pressure not tabulated; text example: 6.3279-fold SSW at 200 C has vapor pressure 197.1942 psia, equal to that of pure water at 193.668 C.

value2.col: Boiling Temperature for Pure Water Tb (C)
value2.what: saturation temperature of pure water at the solution vapor pressure (steam tables)

composition.other_species: Simulated sea water of Na+, Mg2+, Cl-, SO4 2- only. Concentrate multiple f of the Table 11 composition (molal basis, per kg H2O; unit concentration ratio): NaCl 0.42663, Na2SO4 0.02976, MgCl2 0.06726 mol/kg H2O (ions: Na+ 0.48615, Mg2+ 0.06726, Cl- 0.56115, SO4 2- 0.02976). Molality of each salt = f x the Table 11 value. Table 11 itself is the composition used experimentally (analysed; MgCl2 about 4% above the intended Table 10 value).

conversion_needs: molality = multiple x Table 11 salt molalities
notes: Derived by the authors from the Table 12 vapor pressure lowerings with steam-table interpolation (Keenan and Keyes); same 27 solutions as Table 12. Solution temperature filled down.
